title: The gift of self (Gaudium et Spes 24)
hookLine: we find ourselves only through a sincere gift of self
tomorrow: where do all of us come from, and where are we all headed?

lines: A SOLO TRIP TO FIND YOURSELF.
cards: Gap years. Journaling prompts. A solo trip to find yourself.

The self usually gets pictured as something lost, waiting to be found by looking inward, and only then spent on other people. Gaudium et Spes has one line that runs the other way, and it closes the week.
The order it gives is backwards from the poster on the dorm wall.

teach.b: Paragraph twenty-four begins with family. God, it says, cares for everyone like a father, and wants all people to be one family, treating one another as brothers and sisters.

teach.h: THAT THEY ALL MAY BE ONE.
teach.b: Then it turns to Jesus at the Last Supper, praying, in John's Gospel: "That they all may be one, as thou, Father, in me, and I in thee."
The council sees a likeness there, between the unity of God's own life and the unity people can have in truth and love. And from that likeness comes the line.

The human person, the only creature on earth God willed for its own sake, cannot fully find itself except through a sincere gift of self. Two words carry the weight. Sincere: not a performance, not a trade.
Self: not only money, but time, attention, presence. And the order is the surprise. Not find yourself, then give.
Give, and that's where the finding happens.
Look back and the week was full of it: parents handing on faith at a table, a mother who points away from herself, griefs taken on as one's own.

how: Catholic teaching often returns to this line from Gaudium et Spes when it speaks about marriage, family, service and vocation.

games.q: what does “the gift of self” mean?
o: a talent or skill that God gives each person
finding yourself by sincerely giving yourself away
a present you buy for yourself as a reward

games.q: the gift of self — tap the pairs.
p: what God wills all people to be
not a performance or a trade
how a person fully finds themselves

s: Gaudium et Spes 24 says to find yourself first, and then give
it flips it: a person finds themselves through a sincere gift of self.
the paragraph reads Jesus' prayer that all may be one
John 17: a likeness between God's unity and ours.
a sincere gift of self means giving money or things
self: time, attention, presence; not a trade or a performance.

games.q: your older brother says he'll start volunteering "once my life is sorted out." what does Gaudium et Spes 24 suggest about the order?
o: sort life out first; then there's something to give.
give only where someone will notice and thank you.
give sincerely now; that's how the self gets found.
games.why: the council says a person cannot fully find themselves except through a sincere gift of self. the giving isn't the reward for finding; it's the way.

practice: Count on your fingers the people who gave you some of themselves this week: a ride, a meal, someone who listened longer than they had to. Give each one a breath of thanks as the finger goes down. If you reach ten, keep going.

wordCard.voice: The gift of self. Gaudium et Spes 24: a person fully finds themselves only by sincerely giving themselves.

orig.note: Latin for gift, the word in the council's sincere gift of self.

carryVoice: Hold onto this: found by giving, not by holding back. One more week of the council's pages, done.
